definitions.explanation: A tall grass that grows in wetlands, along rivers, and in marshy areas. Used historically for thatching, mat-making, and as a literary symbol.

examples.japanese: ⟦{川辺|かわべ}→川辺：20224_kawabe⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{葦|あし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{茂|しげ}っている→茂る：03924_shigeru⟧。
examples.english: Reeds are growing thick along the riverbank.
When the wind blew, the reeds all swayed together.

examples.japanese: パスカル⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧「⟦{人間|にんげん}→人間：03523_ningen⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{考|かんが}える→考える：00856_kangaeru⟧{葦|あし}⟦である→である：09855_dearu⟧」⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{残|のこ}した→残す：01975_nokosu⟧。
examples.english: Pascal left the famous words, 'Man is a thinking reed.'

notes:
Also read as ⟦よし→よし：10741_yoshi⟧. The alternate reading ⟦よし→よし：10741_yoshi⟧ arose because あし sounds like {悪|あ}し (bad), so the euphemistic reading ⟦よし→よし：10741_yoshi⟧ ({良|よ}し, good) was adopted. Both readings are correct.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {葦|あし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{茂|しげ}る→茂る：03924_shigeru⟧ (reeds grow thick)
- {葦原|あしはら} (reed field, reed bed)
- {葦|あし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{葉|は}→葉：02241_ha⟧ (reed leaves)
- {葦簀|よしず} (reed screen/blind — note: usually read よしず)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The phrase ⟦{考|かんが}える→考える：00856_kangaeru⟧{葦|あし} (thinking reed) from Pascal's Pensées is widely known in Japan. {葦原|あしはら} also appears in classical texts as part of {葦原|あしはら}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{中|なか}つ{国|くに}, an ancient name for Japan.
